classification.difficultyReason: Combine routine exponent manipulation with asymptotes and intercept calculations, using logarithms where intercepts are not integer powers.

content.prompt: Sketch the graph of the following.

answer.short: Increasing exponential with horizontal asymptote $y=-3$, $x$-intercept $(\log_2 3,0)$ and $y$-intercept $(0,-2)$.
answer.worked:
Horizontal asymptote: $y=-3$.

$x$-intercept:
$$\begin{align*}2^x-3&=0\\2^x&=3\\x&=\log_2 3\end{align*}$$
$y$-intercept:
$$\begin{align*}y&=2^0-3\\y&=-2\end{align*}$$
The graph increases and approaches $y=-3$ from above as $x\to-\infty$.

spec.description: Increasing exponential with dashed asymptote y=-3 and labelled exact intercepts.

answer.short: Increasing exponential with horizontal asymptote $y=-5$, $x$-intercept $(\log_3 5,0)$ and $y$-intercept $(0,-4)$.
answer.worked:
Horizontal asymptote: $y=-5$.

$x$-intercept:
$$\begin{align*}3^x-5&=0\\3^x&=5\\x&=\log_3 5\end{align*}$$
$y$-intercept:
$$\begin{align*}y&=3^0-5\\y&=-4\end{align*}$$
The graph increases and approaches $y=-5$ from above as $x\to-\infty$.

spec.description: Increasing exponential with dashed asymptote y=-5 and labelled exact intercepts.

answer.short: Increasing exponential with horizontal asymptote $y=1$ and $y$-intercept $(0,\frac43)$; no $x$-intercept.
answer.worked:
Using index laws:
$$\begin{align*}y&=3^{x-1}+1\\y&=\frac13\,3^x+1\end{align*}$$
Horizontal asymptote: $y=1$.

Since $3^{x-1}>0$, $y>1$, so there is no $x$-intercept.

$y$-intercept:
$$\begin{align*}y&=3^{-1}+1\\y&=\frac43\end{align*}$$
The graph increases and approaches $y=1$ from above as $x\to-\infty$.

spec.description: Increasing exponential above the dashed asymptote y=1, with y-intercept 4/3.
spec.mathematics: y=3^(x-1)+1=(1/3)3^x+1; asymptote y=1; y-intercept (0,4/3); no x-intercept.

answer.short: Decreasing exponential with horizontal asymptote $y=-1$, $x$-intercept $(1,0)$ and $y$-intercept $(0,e-1)$.
answer.worked:
Using index laws:
$$\begin{align*}y&=e^{1-x}-1\\y&=e\,e^{-x}-1\end{align*}$$
Horizontal asymptote: $y=-1$.

$x$-intercept:
$$\begin{align*}e^{1-x}-1&=0\\e^{1-x}&=1\\1-x&=0\\x&=1\end{align*}$$
$y$-intercept:
$$\begin{align*}y&=e^{1-0}-1\\y&=e-1\end{align*}$$
The negative exponent gives a decreasing graph, approaching $y=-1$ from above as $x\to\infty$.

spec.description: Decreasing exponential above the dashed asymptote y=-1, crossing the y-axis at e-1 and the x-axis at 1.
spec.mathematics: y=e^(1-x)-1=e e^(-x)-1; asymptote y=-1; intercepts (1,0) and (0,e-1).
